h: Jacob Attains Wholeness through the Holiness of Shabbat

p: "וַיָּבֹא יַעֲקֹב שָׁלֵם וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לג, יח).
— And Jacob came whole... and he encamped before the city (Genesis 33:18).
וְאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה עט, ו):
— And it is taught in Bereishit Rabbah (79:6):
"נִכְנַס בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת עִם דִּמְדּוּמֵי חַמָּה וְקָבַע תְּחוּמִין מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
— "Jacob entered Shechem on the eve of Shabbat at sunset, establishing the Shabbat boundaries while it was yet day;
הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב: 'וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר' – שֶׁשָּׁמַר יַעֲקֹב אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי".
— this is what is written: 'and he encamped (va-yichan) before the city'—teaching that Jacob observed the Sabbath, etc."
וּלְמַעְלָה בְּפָרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית (פָּרָשָׁה יא, ז) אִיתָא עַל זֶה:
— And earlier in Bereishit Rabbah (11:7) it is stated on this:
"אַבְרָהָם שֶׁאֵין כָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי, אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'וַיִּחַן וְגוֹמֵר'".

— "Abraham, concerning whom explicit Sabbath observance is not written, inherited the world with measure; but Jacob, concerning whom Sabbath observance is explicitly written, inherited without measure."
וְהַיְינוּ דִּבְאַבְרָהָם כָּתוּב רַק בְּרֶמֶז:
— Meaning that regarding Abraham it is written only by broad allusion:
"עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם בְּקֹלִי וַיִּשְׁמֹר מִשְׁמַרְתִּי מִצְוֹתַי חֻקּוֹתַי וְתוֹרֹתָי" (שָׁם כו, ה),
— “Because Abraham hearkened to My voice, and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws,”
שֶׁקִּיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ וְשַׁבָּת בִּכְלָל;
— implying that he fulfilled the entire Torah, including Shabbat;
אֲבָל בְּיַעֲקֹב כָּתוּב בּוֹ מְפוֹרָשׁ "וַיִּחַן וְגוֹמֵר", שֶׁקָּבַע תְּחוּמִין.
— whereas regarding Jacob it is recorded explicitly in the narrative: "and he encamped," showing that he instituted techum Shabbat.

p: וְהוּא כְּעִנְיַן מַאֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רוּת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ה, ו):
— And this parallels what our Sages of blessed memory stated (Ruth Rabbah 5:6):
"שֶׁאִלּוּ הָיָה רְאוּבֵן יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַכְתִּיב עָלָיו: 'וַיִּשְׁמַע רְאוּבֵן וַיַּצִּילֵהוּ מִיָּדָם' (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, כא), עַל כְּתֵפוֹ הָיָה מוֹלִיכוֹ אֵצֶל אָבִיו;
— "Had Reuben known that the Holy One would inscribe concerning him: 'And Reuben heard, and delivered him out of their hand,' he would have carried Joseph on his shoulders to his father;

וְאִלּוּ הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ אַהֲרֹן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַכְתִּיב עָלָיו: 'הִנֵּה הוּא יוֹצֵא לִקְרָאתֶךָ וְרָאֲךָ וְשָׂמַח בְּלִבּוֹ' (שְׁמוֹת ד, יד), בְּתֻפִּים וּבִמְחוֹלוֹת הָיָה יוֹצֵא לִקְרָאתוֹ;

— and had Aaron known that the Holy One would inscribe of him: 'behold, he comes forth to meet you, and when he sees you, he will be glad in his heart,' he would have greeted Moses with timbrels and dancing;
וְאִלּוּ הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ בֹּעַז שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַכְתִּיב עָלָיו: 'וַיִּצְבָּט לָהּ קָלִי' (רוּת ב, יד), עֲגָלִים פְּטוּמִים הָיָה מַאֲכִילָהּ", עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּבֵיאוּרוֹ.
— and had Boaz known that the Holy One would inscribe of him: 'and he reached her parched corn,' he would have fed Ruth fatted calves," see there.
וּבְוַדַּאי שֶׁאֵין הַכַּוָּנָה לְהִתְפָּאֵר בָּזֶה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם;
— And certainly the Midrash does not mean that they would have done so for self-glorification, Heaven forbid;
רַק מִי שֶׁנִּכְתַּב עָלָיו בַּתּוֹרָה מְפוֹרָשׁ, הוּא לְאוֹת שֶׁנִּקְנָה בּוֹ לְקִיּוּם לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד,
— rather, an action explicitly recorded in the eternal Torah serves as testimony that this virtue was acquired by him as an enduring, everlasting acquisition,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַלֵּב נַעֲשָׂה מְזוּכָּךְ בְּעִנְיָן זֶה.
— because the person's heart was completely purified within that specific realm.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת שֶׁנִּזְכַּר אֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מְפוֹרָשׁ:
— And this is the meaning of Sabbath observance being explicitly written concerning our father Jacob:
שֶׁהוּא שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה לִבּוֹ מְזוּכָּךְ בִּקְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת,
— that his heart became totally purified in the sanctity of Shabbat,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּקְשַׁר בִּפְנִימִיּוּת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְזֶה עִנְיַן שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת.
— meaning that his innermost thoughts were continuously bound to Hashem, which is the essence of Shabbat observance.

So I heard from my holy master on the teaching (Berakhot 6a) that when two sit and occupy themselves with Torah, their words are written in a book of remembrance, as it is said, ‘Then those who feared Hashem spoke one to another, and Hashem listened and heard, and it was written in a book of remembrance before Him.’ That is, when a person reveals some word of Torah to his fellow with a favorable intention, it spreads and becomes engraved in the whole of Israel's souls, which are called the ‘book of remembrance’ … How much more so when the deed is written in Scripture or in the words of the Sages: a lesson certainly goes out from it, to be engraved in the souls of Israel forever. p: שֶׁבְּנֵי נֹחַ נִצְטַוּוּ: "יוֹם וָלַיְלָה לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית ח, כב; סַנְהֶדְרִין נח עַמּוּד ב),
— For the Noahides were commanded: "day and night they shall not cease (rest)",
כִּי אִם הוֹלֵךְ בָּטֵל, הֵם אוֹכְלִים וְשׁוֹתִים וּפוֹחֲזִים,
— because if a gentile is idle, he falls into eating, drinking, and reckless decadence,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "אָדָם לְעָמָל יוּלָּד" (אִיּוֹב ה, ז).
— concerning which it is said: "man is born to toil."
אָמְנָם גַּם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֱמַר "אָדָם לְעָמָל יוּלָּד",
— However, regarding Israel it is likewise said that "man is born to toil",
וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶם שְׁנֵי סוּגֵי אֲנָשִׁים:
— and among them exist two categories of people:
שֶׁיֵּשׁ נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁשָּׁרְשָׁם בְּתוֹלָדָה לִהְיוֹת עוֹסְקִים בְּכָל יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בַּעֲמַל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ עִם קְבִיעוּת עִתִּים לַתּוֹרָה,
— there are souls whose innate root is to be engaged during the weekdays in earning a livelihood, while establishing fixed times for Torah,
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ב מִשְׁנָה ב): "יָפֶה תַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה עִם דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וְכוּלֵי",
— as taught in Avot (2:2): "Excellent is the study of Torah combined with a worldly occupation, etc.",
וּכְעִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת לה עַמּוּד ב): "הַרְבֵּה עָשׂוּ כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְעָלְתָה בְּיָדָן, כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדָן";
— and as stated in Berakhot (35b): "Many acted like Rabbi Ishmael (combining work and Torah) and succeeded, whereas many acted like Rashbi (exclusively studying Torah) and did not succeed";
וְזֶה נַעֲשָׂה לוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת הַשְּׁבִיתָה וְהַנְּיָיחָא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
— and for this person, the cessation and rest of Shabbat are dedicated to immersing in words of Torah.
וּמִי שֶׁזָּכָה שֶׁגַּם בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה עֲמָלוֹ בַּעֲמַל תּוֹרָה,
— And one who merits that even during the six workdays his toil is exclusively in the toil of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין צט עַמּוּד ב): "טוּבֵיהּ לִדְזָכֵי דְּהָוֵי דְּרוֹפְתְּקֵי דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא",
— as stated in Sanhedrin (99b): "Happy is he who merits to be a vessel of Torah",
אֲזַי כְּשֶׁבָּא הַשַּׁבָּת, מַרְגִּישׁ קְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת,
— then when Shabbat arrives, he experiences the transcendent sanctity of Shabbat,
שֶׁפְּנִימִיּוּת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ נִקְשָׁר בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֹא שׁוּם פְּעֻלָּה, כִּי כָּל תְּנוּעוֹתָיו הֵמָּה קְשׁוּרִים בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— wherein his innermost mind is bound to Hashem without needing any external action, all his movements being inherently cleaving unto Him.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן קְדוּשַׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בִּשְׁלֵימוּת קְדוּשָׁתוֹ, שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה מְקוּשָּׁר בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל עִנְיָנָיו.
— And this was the holiness of Jacob our father once he reached his absolute spiritual perfection, being bound to Hashem in all his affairs.

— And as our Sages taught (Shabbat 33b) on "And Jacob came whole (shalem)":
"שָׁלֵם בְּגוּפוֹ, שָׁלֵם בְּמָמוֹנוֹ, שָׁלֵם בְּתוֹרָתוֹ".
— "whole in his body, whole in his wealth, whole in his Torah."
וְהַמְּכוּוָּן עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה עִנְיְנֵי הַשְּׁלֵימוּת שֶׁנִּשְׁלְמוּ בָּהֶם שְׁלֹשָׁה הָאָבוֹת,
— And this points to the three dimensions of perfection completed through the three Patriarchs,
אֲשֶׁר בָּזֶה נִשְׁלַם תַּכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה הַפְּגָמִים שֶׁהֵם "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה": קִנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה, וְכָבוֹד
— whereby Creation was rectified from the three primordial flaws of envy, lust, and honor
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיֵּרָא סוֹף מַאֲמָר א):
— (as explained in Vayera, end of Discourse 1):

p: "שָׁלֵם בְּגוּפוֹ" – הוּא הַבֵּירוּר מִמִּדַּת הַקִּנְאָה;
— "Whole in his body"—this is the total purification from the trait of envy;
וְעַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת קנב עַמּוּד ב) בְּרַב אַחַאי בַּר יֹאשִׁיָּה,
— based on Shabbat (152b) regarding Rabbi Achai bar Yoshiyah:
שֶׁכָּל מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קִנְאָה בְּלִבּוֹ אֵין עַצְמוֹתָיו מַרְקִיבִין;
— that whoever harbors no envy in his heart, his bones never rot in the grave (Proverbs 14:30);
וּכְנִרְאֶה מִתּוֹסָפוֹת (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יז עַמּוּד א, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "שִׁבְעָה")
— and as evident from Tosafot (Bava Batra 17a):
שֶׁמִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קִנְאָה גַּם בְּשַׂר הַגּוּף בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, וּכְנִרְאֶה מִלְּשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא "גַּשְׁשֵׁיהּ וְכוּלֵי";
— that for one free of envy, even the flesh of his body remains completely preserved, as seen from the Talmud's account of touching the flesh of Rabbi Achai;
וְעַל כֵּן חִילְּקוּ בְּתוֹסָפוֹת:
— and therefore Tosafot resolved:
דְּהָנָךְ שִׁבְעָה שֶׁלֹּא שָׁלְטָה בָּהֶן רִמָּה – הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה שׁוּם שְׁלִיטָה לְהָרִמָּה,
— that the seven righteous figures over whom worms had no power suffered not the slightest touch of decay,
אֲפִילּוּ כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּנָפַק רִיחְשָׁא מֵאוּדְנֵיהּ (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פד עַמּוּד ב),
— unlike Rabbi Eleazar son of Rashbi from whose ear a tiny worm emerged because he once heard an insult and remained silent;
אֲבָל וַדַּאי שֶׁמִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קִנְאָה נִשְׁאָר כָּל בְּשַׂר הַגּוּף שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַרְקִיב, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— yet certainly whoever is entirely cleansed of envy retains his flesh intact without decay, see there.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן "שָׁלֵם בְּגוּפוֹ" – שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר כָּל גּוּפוֹ בְּקִיּוּם הַשְּׁלֵימוּת עַל יְדֵי בֵּירוּר מִמִּדַּת קִנְאָה.
— And this is "whole in his body"—his physical body remaining preserved in perfection through the total purging of envy.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 17a: “The Sages taught: There were seven people over whom the worm and the maggot had no sway, and they are: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Moses, Aaron and Miriam, and Benjamin, son of Jacob. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as it is written with regard to them, respectively: ‘With everything,’ ‘from everything,’ ‘everything.’ Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, as it is written with regard to them: ‘By the mouth of the Lord’; Benjamin, son of Jacob, as it is written: ‘And to Benjamin he said: The beloved of the Lord, he shall dwell in safety by Him’ (Deuteronomy 33:12). Even in death, he rests securely, unbothered by worms. And some say that even David is included, as it is written: ‘My flesh also dwells secure’ (Psalms 16:9). The Gemara asks: And how does the other authority, who does not include David, explain this? כִּי מָמוֹן שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַתַּאֲווֹת,

— as it is written: "and your silver and your gold is multiplied... then your heart be lifted up, and you forget Hashem your God" (Deuteronomy 8:13–14).

p: "וְשָׁלֵם בְּתוֹרָתוֹ" – הוּא תַּכְלִית הַבֵּירוּר שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— "And whole in his Torah"—this is the ultimate attainment of our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד בַּקָּשַׁת הַכָּבוֹד בְּ"זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" שֶׁהוּא הַגַּאֲוָה;
— which stands counter to the pursuit of honor in the realm of evil, namely pride;
וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּמְשְׁלָה לְמַיִם שֶׁמַּנִּיחִין מָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ וְהוֹלְכִים לְמָקוֹם נָמוּךְ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תַּעֲנִית ז עַמּוּד א).
— and facing it is Torah, compared to water that leaves high places and flows to the lowest ground (Ta'anit 7a).
וְזֶה קְדוּשַׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, שֶׁאָמַר: "קָטֹנְתִּי מִכֹּל הַחֲסָדִים" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לב, יא);
— And this was the holiness of Jacob who declared: "I am unworthy of all the mercies" (Genesis 32:11);
וְעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר: "כָּבוֹד חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ" (מִשְׁלֵי ג, לה),
— and of him it is said: "The wise shall inherit honor" (Proverbs 3:35),
וְאֵין כָּבוֹד אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (חֻלִּין קלג עַמּוּד א),
— and honor is nothing other than Torah (Chullin 133a),
שֶׁכָּל הַמַּשְׁפִּיל עַצְמוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַגְבִּיהוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֵירוּבִין יג עַמּוּד ב),
— for whoever humbles himself, the Holy One elevates (Eruvin 13b),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קכב עַמּוּד ב): "מַאן דְּאִיהוּ זְעֵיר – אִיהוּ רַב".
— as written in the Zohar: "He who is small—he is great."
וּבְיַעֲקֹב נִשְׁלַם תַּכְלִית הַבֵּירוּר בִּשְׁלֵימוּת בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עִנְיָנִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל.
— And in Jacob the ultimate clarification was completed across all three dimensions.

p: וְעֵשָׂו הָיָה תַּכְלִית הַהֵיפֶךְ,
— Whereas Esau was the absolute opposite,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טז עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁעָבַר עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת, וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים,
— transgressing idolatry, illicit relations, and murder,
שֶׁהֵם מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה פְּגָמִים: קִנְאָה, תַּאֲוָה, וְכָבוֹד:
— which derive from the three corruptions of envy, lust, and pride:
שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים – בָּא מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקִּנְאָה וְהַכַּעַס;
— murder stems from envy and wrath;
תַּאֲוָה – גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת;
— illicit relations stem from lust;
וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה – בָּא מִגַּאֲוָה וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת,
— and idolatry stems from arrogance and haughtiness,
עַד שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהִתְגָּאוֹת עַל הַכֹּל וְלִהְיוֹת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
— aspiring to lift himself above all and become a god,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּנְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר: "אֶעֱלֶה עַל בָּמֳתֵי עָב אֶדַּמֶּה לְעֶלְיוֹן" (יְשַׁעְיָה יד, יד).
— as written of Nebuchadnezzar: "I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High" (Isaiah 14:14).

p: וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּשֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה שְׁלֵימוּת הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל,
— And our father Jacob, having attained perfection in these three attributes,
בָּא לִקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, וְנִכְתַּב עָלָיו בַּתּוֹרָה: "וַיִּחַן וְגוֹמֵר".
— arrived at the complete sanctity of Shabbat, concerning which the Torah inscribed of him: "and he encamped (va-yichan)."
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (עט, א) מֵבִיא עַל פָּסוּק "וַיָּבֹא יַעֲקֹב שָׁלֵם" מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר:
— And in Bereishit Rabbah (79:1) it cites on "And Jacob came whole" the verse:
"בְּשֵׁשׁ צָרוֹת יַצִּילֶךָּ וּבְשֶׁבַע לֹא יִגַּע בְּךָ רָע" (אִיּוֹב ה, יט),
— “In six troubles He shall deliver you, and in seven no evil shall touch you” (Job 5:19),
שֶׁזֶּה מְרַמֵּז עַל שְׁלֵימוּת קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בְּשָׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת שֶׁל הָאָבוֹת:
— which alludes to the perfection of Shabbat after completing the three attributes of the Patriarchs:
כִּי "שֵׁשׁ צָרוֹת" – נֶגֶד שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
— for "six troubles" corresponds to the six weekdays,
שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד בֵּירוּר שֵׁשׁ הַמִּדּוֹת
— which parallel the refinement of the six emotional attributes (Ze'ir Anpin),
(שָׁלֹשׁ הֵם כְּנֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת שֶׁהֵם מֶרְכָּבָה לָהֶם, וּבָהֶם נִכְלְלוּ הַשָּׁלֹשׁ הַמִּסְתַּעֲפִים מֵהֶם כַּיָּדוּעַ);
— (three embodying the Patriarchs as their chariot, and three branching forth from them as is known);
וּלְאַחַר שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בָּהֶם, בָּאִים לִבְחִינַת קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
— and once perfected within them, one ascends to the sanctity of Shabbat,
וְהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם.
— which is the overt revelation of the Kingdom of Heaven (Malchut).
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וּבְשֶׁבַע לֹא יִגַּע בְּךָ רָע" –
— And concerning this it is stated: "and in the seventh no evil shall touch you"—
שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית שְׁלֵימוּת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה,
— which is the ultimate apex of holiness,
שֶׁכְּבָר אֵין שְׁלִיטָה בִּבְחִינַת הַהֵיפֶךְ בְּשׁוּם שֶׁמֶץ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
— wherein the opposing side holds no dominion or touch of defilement whatsoever, as stated above:

Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vayishlach 10:3: “On the verse ‘And Jacob came whole … and he encamped before the city’: as it says earlier that when Jacob left, the city's splendor and radiance departed, so now grace returned to the Land of Israel with the coming of Jacob the righteous. And in the Midrash: ‘In six troubles He will deliver you, and in seven no evil will touch you.’ For the six days of work are a preparation for Shabbat. They are called days of labor, in which a person must labor both in material matters and in spiritual ones, the service of the heart, all as a preparation for Shabbat, so as to enter and receive Shabbat in rest. Likewise the days of this world are a preparation for the World to Come, and likewise our father's going out of the Land was a preparation for returning to the Land of Israel in rest. Of this it is written, ‘and he encamped before the city,’ which, as the Midrash says, alludes to Shabbat. … Therefore a person must bring himself under the yoke of labor, so that ‘in seven no evil will touch you’ may be fulfilled.”
